Welcome to

ALTÆR

a modern church

A place to meet God, and to meet Him together.

Why we began

Born out of what went wrong.

Altær grew out of the failures of other churches. Many of us have sat in congregations where decisions were made behind closed doors and explained poorly, or not explained at all.

When leaders decide badly or communicate poorly, relationships pay for it. Trust thins, people stop speaking honestly, and they drift from one another and sometimes from God.

We began Altær to do that part differently. We will make our own mistakes, and when we do we intend to say so plainly. The five convictions below are our answer to what we saw.

Five convictions

A new church, built on five things.

Altær is a modern church with an old shape. These five convictions decide how we lead, how we worship, and how we spend our time.

  1. i

    Relationships come first: God, then each other.

    Everything we do is meant to deepen two relationships. Our relationship with God comes first, and our relationship with one another follows from it. If something serves neither, we leave it out.

  2. ii

    We pursue a shared vision.

    The direction of this church belongs to the people in it. We seek it together, with many voices in the room, and we take the time to listen before we move.

  3. iii

    Pastors and elders decide together.

    No single voice stands at the center of Altær. Several pastors serve in different roles, and each shares responsibility for how our ministries are run. They make decisions together with a board of five elders, with the congregation involved.

  4. iv

    Worship is honest and peaceful.

    We come as we are and we do not perform. Our worship is unhurried and quiet enough to pray in, with room for stillness alongside song.

  5. v

    Transparency is key.

    Decisions, finances, and direction are shared openly with the congregation. Nothing that shapes the life of the church is kept behind closed doors.

How we are led

Leadership is shared here.

Altær has several pastors, each with a different role, and a board of five elders. All of them decide together, so the church never depends on one voice or one personality.

Pastors

Different roles, one shared charge

Our pastors serve in different roles. Each one carries responsibility for how the ministries of the church are run, and none leads alone.

Five elders

A board that shares the decisions

A board of five elders sits with the pastors. Decisions are made by all of them together.

Congregation

A people with a real voice

The congregation is involved in the life and direction of the church. Taking part is expected and welcome.

And they continued stedfastly in the apostles’ doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers. Acts 2:42 · KJV
